title: Add an additive machine-readable review-report action output
problem: The normal PR-review path exposes only the prose review-summary output. ReviewResult already carries findings, status, risk, counts, coverage and diagnostics internally, but no consumer can read them without parsing a human-readable sentence or scraping the PR comment.
hypothesis: Serializing a copy of the validated ReviewResult into a versioned JSON action output closes the integration gap without changing any input, permission, or existing output, and without mutating the engine result.
alternative_solutions: Ask consumers to parse review-summary prose; rejected because it does not expose status, coverage, or per-finding data reliably
Publish the report as an artifact file instead of an output; rejected because it requires consumers to add upload/download steps and the frozen contract permits additive outputs directly
Adopt the competitor's automatic thread resolution instead; rejected because it requires contents:write, above this repository's documented least-privilege contract
confidence_rationale: The implementation side is strongly evidenced: the review result model already carries every serialized field (src/types/finding.ts), runReview sets completion status (src/review/reviewer.ts), and the frozen contract explicitly permits additive outputs (docs/v1-interface-contract.md). Held below 1.0 because the demand side rests on one public competitor issue plus a competitor's shipped feature, and this repository has no direct user reports.
score_band: PROTOTYPE (55-74 raw). Raw 73/100 falls in the PROTOTYPE band, so this is a prototype slice rather than a BUILD commitment.
authorization: The user explicitly authorized this bounded implementation for both the ideation and the implementation, so the prototype proceeds now. That authorization covers local implementation, tests, docs and research artifacts only; it is not a broader roadmap commitment and does not authorize push, release, merge, or any permission change.
why_build: Small additive diff with no new dependency, no new input, and no permission change; the frozen contract explicitly allows additive outputs; the competitor demonstrates a machine-readable review result is a real consumer need. The user explicitly requested both the ideation and this bounded implementation slice, which authorizes the work.
why_not_build: Differentiation is low: the competitor already ships a JSON review output, so this is parity rather than a differentiator. No measured demand exists in this repository's own user base, and one public issue is a single signal. It does not improve review quality or accuracy, only the machine-readability and honesty of what the review already produces.
counterevidence: Issue #367 is one public demand signal from one project's community; it is not proof of broad market demand and says nothing about willingness to pay.
The issue was closed via PR #520, but the closure was not read line-by-line, so whether it fully ships the requested manifest is INFERRED, not verified.
No head-to-head quality, cost, or latency benchmark against the competitor was run; the comparison is capability-shaped, not outcome-shaped.
Competitor README architecture claims are marketing surfaces and were not independently reproduced.
acceptance_criteria: The action exposes an additive review-report output whose JSON shape is versioned with schemaVersion 1
status is derived conservatively from ReviewResult and a failed review group can never serialize as complete
coverage carries filesReviewed, filesTotal, filesExcluded and filesTruncated; counts and risk are present for a clean review
findings, diagnostics and ruleCoverage serialize when present
Every string value is pattern-redacted on a serialized copy and the engine result is not mutated
No input, output value, permission, or existing behavior changes; no new dependency
Skipped, security-mode and failed-before-review runs may leave the output empty, and that is documented
human_decision: Authorized for bounded local implementation, tests, docs and research artifacts by the user's explicit request for both ideation and implementation. Push, release, merge and any permission change remain separately gated.
what_would_change_conclusion: Evidence that the empty-output behavior or the conservative status derivation misrepresents review state for real consumers, or direct user evidence that consumers need a different artifact (for example a signed immutable manifest or a published file artifact) rather than an action output.
